t: Listen to a talk in a history class.
Today we'll discuss the Industrial Revolution.
This was a period of great change that paved the way for the quality of life we enjoy today.

The Industrial Revolution started in Great Britain around 1760, it reached the United States by the end of that century and parts of continental Europe early in the nineteenth century, and in all of these places it meant a shift from an agricultural economy to one driven by industrialization.
We're talking about moving from manual to machine-based manufacturing and ultimately the rise of the factory system.
It also means the increasing use of steam power, new processes for chemical manufacturing and iron production, and the development of machine tools.
A key development was the Scotsman James Watt's coal-powered steam engine in 1769, not long after these events were set in motion in Great Britain.
The steam engine represented a massive shift in power generation.
Until then, factories had been powered by moving water and had to be located by, say, a river or a waterfall.
Now they could be located anywhere.
Another milestone was a machine called the spinning jenny.
The spinning jenny greatly reduced the amount of labor needed to produce textiles and it helped spur the English cotton manufacturing system.
This rapid change drove waves of workers from the countryside into overcrowded, unsanitary cities.
They faced long hours, low pay, and dangerous conditions, sparking labor movements that would play a central role in the century to come.
